Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Move the book behind the flower
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Does the image show any progress toward moving the book behind the flower, even if the requested placement is not complete?
node.criteria: Pass if the image provides clear evidence of partial progress toward placing the book behind the flower, such as a changed relative position or partial occlusion consistent with that placement, without establishing complete fulfillment. Fail if the image clearly shows no progress toward the requested placement. Unknown if progress cannot be determined from the image.
node.binding: Compare the book’s and flower’s relative positions and occlusion in the edited image; do not count unrelated edits as progress.

node_traces.evidence: The edited image shows the book still separate from the flowers, with no overlap or occlusion indicating it has moved behind a flower. The flowers also appear changed, but that is unrelated to the requested placement.

fulfillment: The node’s current outcome is well supported: in the edited image the book and flowers remain spatially separate, with no overlap or occlusion establishing that the book is behind a flower; the flowers’ changed appearance is unrelated. Preserve the requested-placement criterion and the rule that unrelated edits do not count as progress. For robustness, make the binding explicitly compare the edited image with the source and assess the book’s relative position and visible occlusion by the flower, while allowing partial progress only when the evidence shows movement toward that relation. Keep ambiguous or obscured evidence unresolved rather than treating it as failure. The checks are valid, queried, and high-confidence, with no transport or dependency failure indicated; the aggregate already agrees with the reference, so avoid changes that merely force the label.
